title: Decem Theses VII-VIII: Imperial Acts name neither Variata nor Invariata; oral eating and ubiquity absent — Reformed not excludable
pass_a_gloss: VII. Neither the Recesses, nor the Acts or Edicts of the Empire, make any mention either of the Variata or of the Invariata Augsburg Confession (under these disputed Denominations). VIII. The recent doctrine of certain Evangelicals devoted to the Bergen Formula, concerning oral manducation and the ubiquity of Christ's Body, is found neither in the earlier nor in the more augmented Confession, much less in the same's Repetition and in Philip's Body of Doctrine; Whence neither can the Reformed Associates of the Augsburg Confession, on account of these two dogmas denied, be excluded from the Peace of the Empire.
pass_b_english: VII. Neither Imperial Recesses nor Acts or Edicts ever mention a Variata or Invariata Augsburg Confession under those contested labels.

VIII. The recent teaching of certain Evangelicals bound to the Bergen Formula — oral eating and the ubiquity of Christ's body — is in neither the earlier nor the enlarged Confession, and still less in the Repetitio or in Philip's Corpus Doctrinae.
So the Reformed, as associates of the Augsburg Confession, cannot be shut out of the Imperial Peace for denying those two dogmas.
source_text:
VII.
Nec Recessus, nec Acta Edictave Imperii, vel variatae, vel invariatae Augustanae Confessionis (Sub bisputa Denominationibus) mentionem ullam faciunt.
VIII.
Recens quorundam Evangelicorum, Bergensi Formulae addictorum doctrina, de orali manducatione, & ubiquitate Corporis Christi, nec in priori, nec auctiori Confessione, multò minùs in ejusdem Repetitione & Corpore Doctrinae Philippi reperitur; Unde nec Reformati Augustanae Confessionis Socii, ob haec duo dogmata negata, pace Imperii excludi possunt.
